text:
Florian Wirtz has credited Andoni Iraola with helping him recapture the form that made him one of the most coveted players in Europe when he joined Liverpool in a deal worth up to £116m in 2025.
The Germany international believes he is in the best form of his Liverpool career, having had a difficult debut season under Arne Slot and also struggled in the early weeks of Iraola’s reign. Wirtz scored an exquisite improvised goal in the 4-0 defeat of Manchester United on Sunday when he also created 10 chances from open play.
Speaking in the buildup to Liverpool’s Champions League game against Club Brugge on Wednesday, Wirtz attributed his improvement to becoming “a bit better on a physical level” and gaining a better understanding of English football and the Premier League. The 23-year-old claimed he is back to the heights he reached with Bayer Leverkusen, when Liverpool, Real Madrid and Manchester City all challenged for his services, thanks to working with Iraola.
“I am really enjoying playing under him, he is a really good coach,” said Wirtz in Belgium. “He is bringing me back into the place where I was maybe two years ago where I played really good football. I can feel that he gives me confidence and I am really happy about that. I am just trying to give him back what he gives me.”
Wirtz has scored five goals in his last four games for club and country, also flourishing on international duty with Jürgen Klopp’s Germany. He said the former Liverpool manager has given him advice on how to prove his worth at Anfield.
The playmaker added: “We speak always about Liverpool when we have the time to do so. He had a great time here. He just tells me all the time that he loved his time here, the people love him here, he tries to give me some advice to be successful here because he has shown how it is done. It is small things, more private things. He is just speaking good about the club, the region, the people, and that helps to hear someone who has experienced it.”
Wirtz claimed his fierce self-belief has enabled him to handle criticism since the big-money move from Leverkusen. “It’s mainly a thing that goes on in my own head,” he explained. “It’s not about the people who talk about me. It’s the goals I set myself and the performances I want to show for myself. I always believed in myself. I knew my qualities, and I know them now.
“Sometimes there are phases where you have to work even more to get the output, but I’m just enjoying the moment and really happy that it’s going well. Of course there were days where I wasn’t happy with myself. I always try to work on myself and get better every day but I still believe it makes no sense to put too much pressure on yourself as that doesn’t help in the process to get to where you want. I just believed in myself so I wasn’t too annoyed.”
Liverpool will again be without the injured Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch against Club Brugge, who are second in the Belgian Pro League and won 4-3 at Inter, the Italian champions, last month.
Iraola said: “Sometimes you have to analyse a team and watch a lot of games and it’s a little boring but with Brugge that definitely doesn’t happen. They are a very attractive team. They are very energetic. Everyone runs and they are very aggressive in the press. They are coming in on an incredible run of games – 10 wins and a draw in their last 11. We will have to be at a very good level otherwise, it is going to be very difficult.”
